# Parity fixtures

Real captures that the dissection is measured against, per column, with tshark as
the oracle. Everything in this directory except this file and `acceptance.json` is
**untracked**: the captures carry the author's DNS and SNI history and home addresses,
and so does the ground truth tshark derives from them
(`docs/decisions/0004-fixtures-and-privacy.md`). Keep a copy of the two `.pcap` files
somewhere other than `Downloads/`; they are the only copies.

| name | file | frames | SHA-256 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `inwire` | `inwire_capture_1788478187989.pcap` | 12,858 | `01f184b7ff5f1078460f08e64eb1a3944ffda89f961736488da8abfc2c427937` |
| `bulk` | `bulk_capture_1788426090876.pcap` | 14,782 | `2d20930051c0d1f91e5e40a1413ce5c7c73f432ad0e3f2c609789916a7b432e8` |

Both are Ethernet, snaplen 65535, microsecond timestamps, exported by the app itself.

One more is **optional**: scripts that need it name it, and everything else ignores it
(`OPTIONAL_CAPTURES` in `scripts/export/realCaptures.ts`).

| name | file | frames | SHA-256 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `icmpErrors` | `icmp_errors_capture_1790359378632.pcapng` | 66 | `a8f445db710493c9911e4dfe700b78e5aeaeda515957e9e24c0c5d217268919a` |

Neither general capture holds a single ICMP error, so the anonymiser's rewrite of the
packet an error quotes had nothing real to run against. This is 50 seconds of
Wireshark's `dumpcap -i <Ethernet> -f "icmp or icmp6 or igmp"` while `tracert -d -h 4`
ran to 1.1.1.1 and `tracert -6 -d -h 4` to 2606:4700:4700::1111: 12 ICMPv4 and 9 ICMPv6
Time Exceeded, each quoting the echo that expired, plus Neighbor Solicitations and
Advertisements and one Router Advertisement. pcapng, one interface.
It carries this machine's addresses and MAC like the others, and is untracked for the
same reason.

They are named for what they hold, because a measurement is only comparable if you
know which capture produced it. `inwire` is general browsing - 3,088 QUIC rows, 43
TLS hellos, and most of the TCP analysis this build is held to. `bulk` is long TLS
transfer: 86 QUIC rows, multi-megabyte sequence spaces, and **30 TCP streams with
exactly one SYN between them**, which makes it the one that catches anything
assuming a capture opens with a handshake. It was called `netview` until the app was
renamed; the label moved and the bytes did not, so every number recorded against the
old name still refers to this file.

## Files

- `<name>.pcap` - the capture, named as in `acceptance.json`.
- `<name>.psv`, `<name>-colors.psv` - tshark ground truth, regenerated by
  `./scripts/parity/regen-ground-truth.sh [name]` (two-pass, fields listed in
  `acceptance.json`). Regenerate after upgrading Wireshark and record the version.
- `acceptance.json` - tracked. Per fixture: the file, its hash, the per-column match
  floors the parity check holds the code to, and the counts tshark reports. A count
  is only enforced once its name is in `enforce`; the rest are printed as gaps.
- `acceptance.json`'s `tree` block - what the protocol TREE is held to, which is a
  different question from the columns and is measured by
  `scripts/parity/tree-coverage.ts` (ADR 0039). **Counts, never percentages**: the
  denominator of a coverage ratio is the reference's own vocabulary, so a ratio
  floor would fail on the Wireshark upgrade the line above tells you to perform.
  `layers` and `protosNamed` are floors and may only rise; the two `ceilings` may
  only fall; `counts` is recorded and never enforced; `unimplemented` names a layer
  whose floor is deliberately absent, and an entry may only leave it by becoming a
  floor.

## Running

```
./scripts/parity/regen-ground-truth.sh          # once, and after a Wireshark upgrade
npx tsx scripts/parity/parity-check.ts          # both fixtures, exit 1 on any regression
npx tsx scripts/parity/tree-coverage.ts        # the tree; --write-floors to record it
npx tsx scripts/parity/parity-check.ts inwire   # one
npx tsx scripts/parity/parity-check.ts --write-floors   # after a phase raises a column
```

`--write-floors` records each column's current match percentage (rounded down to one
decimal) as the new floor. Floors are only ever raised; a phase that lowers one has
regressed something and must say why in its gate notes.

Verify a capture before trusting a number:

```
sha256sum test/fixtures/*.pcap
```
